text: If the rear combination lamp is approved as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA) under UN R10, an approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to the approved type. No marking is required if the electronics are built into a vehicle that is approved as a unit.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp as ESA (LED PCBs, wiring and connector); housing marking area
test_case: Visual inspection of production samples and drawings: when ESA approval under UN R10 is held, check that the paragraph 5.3 approval mark is present on every unit of the approved type. Pass if the mark is present on all units. If the lamp is covered only by the vehicle's R10 approval, confirm that this is documented.

text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN Regulation No. 10.
applies_to: LED light sources on PCB(s), internal wiring and electrical connector (whole lamp ESA)
test_case: Design review and fitting check of the lamp ESA as installed on the M1 vehicle. Pass if the ESA passes the UN R10 ESA tests (para. 6.1.1.2) and does not cause the vehicle to fail UN R10 radiated emission or immunity limits under normal conditions of use.

text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for radiated emissions.
applies_to: LED driver electronics on PCB(s) for the rear position, stop and reversing functions, with wiring and connector
test_case: ESA radiated emissions test per UN R10 ESA broadband/narrowband radiated emission annexes, with each function (rear position, stop, reversing) energised. Pass if emissions stay at or below the ESA reference limits.

text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for conducted emissions.
applies_to: LED driver electronics, supply lines and electrical connector to vehicle harness
test_case: ESA conducted emissions test on the supply lines per the relevant UN R10 annexes, with each lighting function energised. Pass if conducted emissions/transients stay within the specified limits.

text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
applies_to: LED light sources and driver electronics for the rear position, stop and reversing functions
test_case: ESA radiated immunity test per the UN R10 ESA immunity annex, with the functions monitored. Pass if there is no degradation of the rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions, e.g. no unintended switching, flicker or loss of light output, at the required field strength.

text: The rear combination lamp, as an ESA, shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
applies_to: LED driver electronics, supply lines and electrical connector
test_case: ESA conducted immunity/transient test on the supply lines per the relevant UN R10 annex, with the functions monitored. Pass if the lighting functions show no malfunction during or after the applied disturbances, according to the agreed functional status.

text: The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear combination lamp ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electronics (LED PCBs, drivers, wiring) as ESA
test_case: Annex 7 ESA radiated broadband emission test performed on a representative sample with all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) operated. Pass if the measurement is performed per the Annex 7 setup and procedure.

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electronics (LED PCBs, drivers, wiring) as ESA
test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement over 30-75 MHz with the lamp functions energised. Pass if all values are below the logarithmically decreasing limit line from 62 dBµV/m at 30 MHz to 52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz (Appendix 6).

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electronics (LED PCBs, drivers, wiring) as ESA
test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement over 75-400 MHz with the lamp functions energised. Pass if all values are below the logarithmically increasing limit line from 52 dBµV/m at 75 MHz to 63 dBµV/m at 400 MHz (Appendix 6).

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electronics (LED PCBs, drivers, wiring) as ESA
test_case: Annex 7 broadband radiated emission measurement over 400-1,000 MHz with the lamp functions energised. Pass if all values are below 63 dBµV/m.

text: On the rear combination lamp ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electronics (LED PCBs, drivers, wiring) as ESA
test_case: Compare the Annex 7 broadband results across 30-1,000 MHz for each operating mode (position, stop, reversing, combined) with the 6.5.2.1 limit curve. Pass if every measured value is strictly below the limit.

text: The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB electronics of the rear combination lamp (ESA)
test_case: Annex 8 narrowband radiated emission measurement on a representative rear combination lamp sample; pass if the measurement is performed per Annex 8 and the results are recorded across 30 to 1,000 MHz.

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB electronics of the rear combination lamp (ESA)
test_case: Annex 8 narrowband emission scan from 30 to 75 MHz with the rear position, stop and reversing functions operating; pass if every narrowband emission is below the logarithmically decreasing limit of 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m (Appendix 7).

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB electronics of the rear combination lamp (ESA)
test_case: Annex 8 narrowband emission scan from 75 to 400 MHz with the lamp functions operating; pass if every narrowband emission is below the logarithmically increasing limit of 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m (Appendix 7).

text: When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB electronics of the rear combination lamp (ESA)
test_case: Annex 8 narrowband emission scan from 400 to 1,000 MHz with the lamp functions operating; pass if every narrowband emission is below 53 dB microvolts/m.

text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (representative sample)
test_case: Compare the Annex 8 narrowband measurement results of the representative sample against the 6.6.2.1 limit curve over 30 to 1,000 MHz; pass if all measured values are below the limits.

text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances on the 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (LED PCBs, internal wiring and connector to vehicle harness)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 transient conducted emission test on the supply lines of a representative sample of the lamp with all functions (rear position, stop, reversing) operated. Pass if the measured pulses stay within the Table 1 limits.

text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA supply lines (12 V system)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on a 12 V supply with each lamp function switched on and off. Pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +75 V.

text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA supply lines (12 V system)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on a 12 V supply with each lamp function switched on and off. Pass if the negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -100 V in magnitude.

text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +150 V.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA supply lines (24 V system, if applicable)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on a 24 V supply with each lamp function switched on and off. Pass if the positive pulse amplitude is ≤ +150 V.

text: For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -450 V.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA supply lines (24 V system, if applicable)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 7637-2 measurement on a 24 V supply with each lamp function switched on and off. Pass if the negative pulse amplitude does not exceed -450 V in magnitude.

text: The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear combination lamp ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (LED PCBs, driver electronics, wiring and connector)
test_case: Annex 9 radiated immunity test using one or more of the stripline, TEM cell, BCI, ALSE or reverberation chamber methods; the test plan and report shall identify the chosen method(s).

text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 60 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the position, stop or reversing functions over more than 90 per cent of the frequency band.

text: When tested by the stripline method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 stripline test, 20 to 400 MHz at 50 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell test, 20 to 200 MHz at 75 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 TEM cell test, 20 to 200 MHz at 62,5 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the BCI method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (harness/connector)
test_case: Annex 9 bulk current injection on the lamp harness, 20 to 400 MHz at 60 mA. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the BCI method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (harness/connector)
test_case: Annex 9 bulk current injection, 20 to 400 MHz at 50 mA. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 absorber-lined shielded enclosure test, 80 to 2,000 MHz at 30 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 80 to 2,000 MHz at 25 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz at 10 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the ALSE method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 ALSE test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz at 8 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 21 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, LUF to 2,000 MHz at 18 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a test level of 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over more than 90 per cent of the band (Table 2a).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz at 7 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions over more than 90 per cent of the band.

text: When tested by the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the rear combination lamp ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range (Table 2b).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Annex 9 reverberation chamber test, 2,000 to 6,000 MHz at 6 V/m. Pass if there is no degradation of the lamp functions at any frequency.

text: During the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions of the rear combination lamp ESA.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions (LED light sources and drivers)
test_case: Monitor each lamp function during all Annex 9 exposures. Pass if there is no unintended switching on or off, no flicker and no change of light output for the position, stop and reversing functions.

text: The immunity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) of ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
applies_to: Whole rear combination lamp ESA (LED PCBs, wiring and connector to the vehicle harness)
test_case: Annex 10 / ISO 16750-2 and ISO 7637-2 conducted transient tests on the supply lines at the Table 3a/3b levels; pass if the test set-up and levels match the regulation.

text: The starting profile test of the rear combination lamp shall be evaluated according to the functional status classification defined in ISO 16750-1.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions during the starting profile test
test_case: Annex 10 starting profile test; pass if the lamp behaviour is classified per ISO 16750-1 and meets the Table 3a status.

text: The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) of ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the rear combination lamp for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions during ISO 7637-2 pulse tests
test_case: Annex 10 pulse tests; pass if the lamp behaviour is classified per ISO 7637-1 FPSC and meets the Table 3b class.

text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions (e.g. stop lamp) that shall be operational during engine start phases shall meet functional status B when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II (12 V and 24 V systems) with 10 pulses.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions (e.g. stop lamp) operational during engine start
test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses, per Annex 10; pass if functional status B per ISO 16750-1.

text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions that need not be operational during engine start phases shall meet functional status C when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions not required during engine start
test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses; pass if functional status C per ISO 16750-1.

text: If the lamp may be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet functional status D when subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses.
applies_to: Lamp functions not related to immunity related functions (e.g. reversing lamp, if so classified)
test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile, level II, 10 pulses; pass if functional status D per ISO 16750-1.

text: When subjected to test pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V system) or -450 V (24 V system) for 500 pulses, the rear combination lamp shall meet FPSC class III, both for functions related and not related to immunity related functions.
applies_to: All lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing)
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 1, -75 V/-450 V, 500 pulses per Annex 10; pass if FPSC III per ISO 7637-1.

text: When subjected to test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class I.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions (e.g. stop lamp)
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a, +37 V, 500 pulses; pass if FPSC I (function performs as designed during and after test).

text: When subjected to test pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V systems) for 500 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class III.
applies_to: Lamp functions not related to immunity related functions
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a, +37 V, 500 pulses; pass if FPSC III.

text: When subjected to test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class II.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions (e.g. stop lamp)
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b, +10 V/+20 V, 10 pulses; pass if FPSC II.

text: When subjected to test pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V system) or +20 V (24 V system) for 10 pulses, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class III.
applies_to: Lamp functions not related to immunity related functions
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b, +10 V/+20 V, 10 pulses; pass if FPSC III.

text: When subjected to test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class I.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions (e.g. stop lamp)
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a, -112 V/-150 V, 1 h; pass if FPSC I.

text: When subjected to test pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V system) or -150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class III.
applies_to: Lamp functions not related to immunity related functions
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a, -112 V/-150 V, 1 h; pass if FPSC III.

text: When subjected to test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the rear combination lamp functions related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class I.
applies_to: Immunity-related lamp functions (e.g. stop lamp)
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b, +75 V/+150 V, 1 h; pass if FPSC I.

text: When subjected to test pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V system) or +150 V (24 V system) for a test duration of 1 h, the rear combination lamp functions not related to immunity related functions shall meet FPSC class III.
applies_to: Lamp functions not related to immunity related functions
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b, +75 V/+150 V, 1 h; pass if FPSC III.

text: Where the ESA (rear combination lamp, including its LED driver electronics) does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8 (radiated narrowband emissions).
applies_to: LED light sources and driver electronics on PCB(s) for rear position, stop and reversing functions
test_case: Design review of the circuit diagram and bill of materials to confirm there is no oscillator, PWM controller, switching regulator or microcontroller clock above 9 kHz. If confirmed, document the exemption from the paragraph 6.6.2. / Annex 8 narrowband test. Otherwise, test according to Annex 8 against the paragraph 6.6.2. limits.

text: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp electrical circuit and connector to the 12/24 V vehicle supply
test_case: Design review to establish whether the lamp is switched, contains switches or includes an inductive load (e.g. switching-regulator inductors). If none applies, document the exemption from the paragraph 6.7. transient conducted emission test. Otherwise, test the 12/24 V supply lines against the paragraph 6.7. limits.

text: The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp, as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly approved under UN R10, shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements of paragraph 9.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp as an ESA (LED PCBs, wiring, connector); manufacturer's production quality system
test_case: Audit of the production quality system and CoP plan against Schedule 1 of E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3 and the paragraph 9 requirements; pass if CoP procedures exist, are applied, and production samples conform to the approved type.

text: The rear combination lamp (ESA) approved under UN R10 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7. of UN R10.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp as ESA (LED PCBs, internal wiring and connector)
test_case: Conformity of production check: series-production samples tested per paragraph 6 (emission and immunity limits per the relevant annexes) and, if applicable, paragraph 7; pass if the samples meet the same limits as the approved type.

text: Conformity of production of the rear combination lamp, approved as a component or separate technical unit (electrical/electronic sub-assembly), shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the communication form for type approval set out in Annex 3B to this Regulation.
applies_to: Complete rear combination lamp as an ESA (LED PCBs, internal wiring and connector)
test_case: Conformity-of-production check: compare production samples against the data recorded in the Annex 3B communication form (e.g. EMC-relevant design and electronics). Pass if production units match the approved data and continue to meet the approved EMC limits.

text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the rear combination lamp ESA shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the broadband electromagnetic disturbance reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1.
applies_to: LED light sources, PCB(s) and wiring of rear position, stop and reversing functions (ESA broadband emission)
test_case: COP sample from series measured per the ESA broadband emission method of the Regulation (Annex 7); pass if measured levels ≤ reference limits of 6.5.2.1. (and 7.10.2.1. if applicable) + 4 dB.

text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the rear combination lamp ESA shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the narrowband electromagnetic disturbance reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1.
applies_to: LED light sources, PCB(s) and wiring of rear position, stop and reversing functions (ESA narrowband emission)
test_case: COP sample from series measured per the ESA narrowband emission method of the Regulation (Annex 8); pass if measured levels ≤ reference limits of 6.6.2.1. + 4 dB.

text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the rear combination lamp ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (ESA radiated immunity)
test_case: COP sample from series tested per the ESA radiated immunity method (Annex 9) at up to 80 % of the field strength limits of 6.8.2.1. (and 7.18.2.1. if applicable); pass if no observable degradation of lamp functions (e.g. no flicker, extinction or unintended activation).

text: When the conformity of a component taken from the series is being verified, the rear combination lamp shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to the conducted disturbance levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions; electrical connector and supply lines (conducted immunity)
test_case: COP sample tested for conducted transient immunity along supply lines per Annex 10 at levels of 6.9.1. (and 7.19.1. if applicable); pass if no degradation of immunity related functions (stop, position, reversing lamp operation).

text: When the conformity of a component taken from the series is being verified, the rear combination lamp shall not exceed the conducted emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.
applies_to: LED driver electronics, PCB(s) and connector supply lines (conducted emission)
test_case: COP sample measured for conducted transient emissions along supply lines per Annex 10 (and harmonic/flicker/RF conducted emission methods if 7.17.1. applies); pass if levels ≤ limits of 6.7.1. (and 7.17.1. if applicable).

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. or 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB(s) / ESA electronics of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing functions)
test_case: Broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 (ESA, 120 kHz bandwidth) across 30-75 MHz with lamp functions energised; pass if all measured values are at or below 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m.

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. or 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB(s) / ESA electronics of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing functions)
test_case: Broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 (ESA, 120 kHz bandwidth) across 75-400 MHz with lamp functions energised; pass if all measured values are at or below 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m.

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.5.2.1. or 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation, the broadband electromagnetic radiation emitted by the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the constant limit E = 63 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB(s) / ESA electronics of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing functions)
test_case: Broadband radiated emission measurement per Annex 7 (ESA, 120 kHz bandwidth) across 400-1,000 MHz with lamp functions energised; pass if all measured values are at or below 63 dBµV/m.

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources on PCB(s) and associated electronics/wiring (ESA)
test_case: ESA narrowband radiated emission measurement per paragraph 6.6.2.1. / Annex 8 method, 120 kHz bandwidth, 30-75 MHz; pass if measured level <= 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m at every frequency

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources on PCB(s) and associated electronics/wiring (ESA)
test_case: ESA narrowband radiated emission measurement per paragraph 6.6.2.1. / Annex 8 method, 120 kHz bandwidth, 75-400 MHz; pass if measured level <= 42 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m at every frequency

text: When measured according to paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, the narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall not exceed the constant limit E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
applies_to: LED light sources on PCB(s) and associated electronics/wiring (ESA)
test_case: ESA narrowband radiated emission measurement per paragraph 6.6.2.1. / Annex 8 method, 120 kHz bandwidth, 400-1,000 MHz; pass if measured level <= 53 dBµV/m at every frequency

text: For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network (AN) as defined in Figure 1 of Appendix 8 shall be used for the conducted emission and immunity test set-ups.
applies_to: LED electronics / electrical connector to vehicle harness (LV power supply lines) of the rear combination lamp during ESA EMC testing
test_case: Inspect the ESA test set-up against Appendix 8 Figure 1. Pass if each LV supply line is connected through a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN (L1 5 µH, C1 0,1 µF, C2 1 µF, R1 1 kΩ).

text: The AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
applies_to: LV power supply test set-up of the rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Visually inspect the test bench. Pass if the AN housings sit directly on the ground plane.

text: The grounding connection of the AN(s) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
applies_to: LV power supply test set-up of the rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Inspect and check the bonding of the AN ground terminal B to the ground plane. Pass if a low-impedance bond is present.

text: Measurement ports of the AN(s) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.
applies_to: LV power supply test set-up of the rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Inspect the AN measuring ports (MEP) during testing. Pass if each port not connected to the receiver is terminated with 50 Ω.

text: The AN impedance ZPB shall correspond to Figure 2 within a tolerance of ± 20 % in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz, when measured between terminals P and B with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and terminals A and B short circuited.
applies_to: Artificial network used for LV supply of the rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Measure ZPB from 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz with the measuring port terminated in 50 Ω and A–B shorted. Pass if the result lies within ± 20 % of the Figure 2 curve.

text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the rear combination lamp (ESA) shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
applies_to: LED light sources, PCBs and wiring of the rear combination lamp (ESA)
test_case: Annex 7 / CISPR 25 radiated broadband emission test; pass if the test setup and procedure follow CISPR 25 except where Annex 7 states otherwise.

text: The rear combination lamp (ESA) under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (LED electronics)
test_case: Check the test report: all lamp functions are energised at nominal supply voltage, preferably all simultaneously at maximum load, during the whole 30-1,000 MHz measurement.

text: For an ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the radiated broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (ESA) with its harness and connector
test_case: Check the setup in the ALSE: lamp, harness and ground plane arranged per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4. As an alternative, an OATS complying with CISPR 16-1-4 is acceptable (Annex 7, 3.3).

text: Measurements of the ambient shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
applies_to: Broadband emission test of the rear combination lamp
test_case: Ambient scan with the lamp unpowered, taken before or after the main test, over 30-1,000 MHz; pass if ambient is ≥6 dB below the para. 6.5.2.1 limits, excluding intentional narrowband transmissions.

text: The broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (ESA) radiated broadband emissions
test_case: Scan 30-1,000 MHz in an ALSE or OATS; pass if emissions are at or below the para. 6.5 limits across the whole range.

text: If peak detectors are used for the broadband emission measurement of the rear combination lamp, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the quasi-peak limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission measurement evaluation
test_case: Review evaluation: peak readings compared against the quasi-peak limit with the 20 dB CISPR 12 correction applied; quasi-peak readings compared directly against the limit.

text: The broadband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver, using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2 of Annex 7.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission measurement instrumentation
test_case: For a spectrum analyser, 30-1,000 MHz: peak RBW 100/120 kHz with minimum scan time 100 ms/MHz; quasi-peak RBW 120 kHz with minimum scan time 20 s/MHz. For a scanning receiver: peak BW 120 kHz, maximum step 60 kHz, minimum dwell 5 ms; quasi-peak BW 120 kHz, maximum step 60 kHz, minimum dwell 1 s. For purely broadband disturbances the step size may be increased up to the bandwidth value.

text: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission measurement instrumentation (FFT-based)
test_case: If an FFT instrument is used, verify it meets CISPR 16-1-1, records continuously, and uses a dwell of at least 1 s per analysis band in real-time mode.

text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check analyser settings: VBW ≥ 3 × RBW for peak scans.

text: Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp harness and connector test layout
test_case: Verify in the setup that the LV harness of the lamp is placed on the side closest to the antenna.

text: The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission test setup
test_case: Measure the antenna position: phase centre is aligned with the midpoint of the longitudinal harness section for 30-1,000 MHz.

text: In the event that the emission limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the rear combination lamp (ESA) and not to background radiation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission test evaluation
test_case: For any exceedance, repeat the measurement with the lamp switched off or compare against the ambient scan to confirm the source.

text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp emission test evaluation
test_case: Measure in both antenna polarizations; for each band, take the worst-case reading relative to the limit as the characteristic reading and compare it with the limit.

text: If not otherwise stated in Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emission test of the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (LED PCBs/drivers, wiring and connector)
test_case: Review the test report against CISPR 25. Pass: the test set-up and procedure conform to CISPR 25 except where Annex 8 states otherwise.

text: During the narrowband emission test, the rear combination lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp LED electronics
test_case: Check the test set-up record. Pass: the lamp functions are energised in normal operation, preferably with all functions (position, stop and reversing) on at maximum load.

text: The narrowband emission test of the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25, or alternatively in an open area test site (OATS) complying with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Verify the test site and arrangement. Pass: an ALSE arrangement per CISPR 25 para. 6.4 is used, or an OATS compliant with CISPR 16-1-4.

text: Ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of the Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
applies_to: Test environment for the rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Measure the ambient with the ESA unpowered, before or after the main test, over 30 to 1,000 MHz. Pass: the ambient is at least 6 dB below the para. 6.6.2.1 limits (intentional narrowband transmissions excepted).

text: The narrowband radiated emissions of the rear combination lamp ESA shall comply with the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Perform a radiated emission scan from 30 to 1,000 MHz per Annex 8. Pass: the emissions are below the para. 6.6.2.1 narrowband limits across the whole range.

text: The narrowband emission measurements of the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed with an average detector.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the instrument settings. Pass: the average detector is selected.

text: The narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the equipment list. Pass: a spectrum analyser or scanning receiver is used; spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments meet CISPR 16-1-1.

text: When a spectrum analyser is used, the average detector measurement from 30 to 1,000 MHz shall use an RBW at -3 dB of 100/120 kHz and a minimum scan time of 100 ms/MHz.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the analyser settings. Pass: RBW is 100/120 kHz (-3 dB) and scan time is at least 100 ms/MHz.

text: When a scanning receiver is used, the average detector measurement from 30 to 1,000 MHz shall use a BW at -6 dB of 120 kHz, a maximum step size of 60 kHz and a minimum dwell time of 5 ms.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the receiver settings. Pass: BW is 120 kHz (-6 dB), step is no more than 60 kHz and dwell is at least 5 ms.

text: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Verify the FFT instrument mode. Pass: gapless real-time recording and evaluation is used.

text: If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the FFT settings. Pass: the measurement time is at least 1 s per analysis band.

text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
applies_to: Measurement instrumentation
test_case: Check the VBW setting. Pass: VBW is at least 3 x RBW.

text: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the rear combination lamp ESA and not to background radiation, including broadband radiation from the ESA.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: For any exceedance, compare against the ambient with the ESA off and against the broadband (peak/QP) characteristics. Pass: the exceedance cause is identified and documented.

text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Measure in both antenna polarisations and take the worst-case reading per band. Pass: the characteristic reading in each band is below the limit.

text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that the results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9: absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5, and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA (LED PCBs, wiring and connector)
test_case: Review the test plan and reports to confirm that the chosen ISO 11452-2/-3/-4/-5/-11 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz. Pass: the full range is covered with no gaps.

text: For the immunity tests of the rear combination lamp ESA, the frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Check the test setup and report against ISO 11452-1. Pass: the frequency range and general conditions conform.

text: The test conditions for the rear combination lamp ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Audit the test conditions (temperature, supply voltage, etc.) against ISO 11452-1. Pass: they conform.

text: The rear combination lamp ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
applies_to: Rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions (LED drivers/PCBs)
test_case: During the immunity test, energise the rear position, stop and reversing functions in normal operating mode. Pass: all functions are active during exposure.

text: The rear combination lamp ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA test arrangement
test_case: Inspect the test arrangement against Annex 9 and the applicable ISO 11452 part. Pass: the arrangement conforms.

text: Any extraneous equipment required to operate the rear combination lamp ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase.
applies_to: Test setup / support equipment
test_case: Verify the calibration records and setup photos. Pass: no ESA support equipment is present during calibration.

text: No extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.
applies_to: Test setup / support equipment
test_case: Measure the distance from the reference point to any equipment during calibration. Pass: the distance is ≥ 1 m.

text: The test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.
applies_to: Test signal generating equipment
test_case: Compare the test-phase equipment and layout with the calibration-phase records. Pass: they are identical.

text: If the rear combination lamp ESA under test consists of more than one unit, the interconnecting cables should ideally be the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle; if these are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
applies_to: Internal wiring and connector / test harness
test_case: Inspect the harness used in the test. Pass: it is the vehicle-intended harness, or the ECU-to-AN length is as defined in the applicable ISO 11452 part.

text: All cables in the wiring harness of the rear combination lamp ESA should be terminated as realistically as possible and preferably with real loads and actuators.
applies_to: Wiring harness / loads (LED loads)
test_case: Inspect the harness terminations. Pass: real or representative loads are connected.

text: Immunity measurements of the rear combination lamp ESA shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Sweep 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes. Pass: no malfunction of the lamp functions.

text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Verify the signal generator settings for 20 to 400 MHz: AM, 1 kHz, 80 % depth. Pass: the settings are applied and the ESA functions remain unaffected.

text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Verify the generator settings for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz: PM, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs. Pass: the settings are applied and there is no malfunction.

text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: Verify the generator settings for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz: PM, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs. Pass: the settings are applied and there is no malfunction.

text: The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA immunity test
test_case: Check the test software's step and dwell settings against ISO 11452-1. Pass: they conform.

text: If the rear combination lamp ESA fails the tests defined in Annex 9, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA
test_case: On failure, check the field and forward-power monitoring for uncontrolled fields. Pass: the failure is confirmed as occurring under the specified conditions.

text: When the absorber chamber test is used, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – absorber chamber test
test_case: Review the ISO 11452-2 calibration records. Pass: the field was established by the substitution method.

text: When the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – absorber chamber test
test_case: Check the antenna orientation during the test. Pass: the polarization is vertical.

text: When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – TEM cell test
test_case: Perform the test per ISO 11452-3. Pass: no malfunction of the lamp functions.

text: When bulk current injection testing is used on a test bench, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 using either the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI closed loop method with the injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – wiring harness / connector (BCI)
test_case: Verify the injection probe position (150 mm for substitution, 900 mm for closed loop) and run the test per ISO 11452-4. Pass: no malfunction.

text: As an alternative to bench BCI testing, the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4, using the BCI substitution method with the injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA installed in the M1 vehicle
test_case: For an in-vehicle BCI test per ISO 11451-4, verify the substitution method with the probe at 150 mm from the ESA. Pass: no malfunction.

text: When stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA wiring harness – stripline test
test_case: Perform the test per ISO 11452-5. Pass: no malfunction of the lamp functions.

text: When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – reverberation chamber test
test_case: Perform the test per ISO 11452-11. Pass: no malfunction.

text: Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing method shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp ESA – reverberation chamber test setup
test_case: Inspect the setup. Pass: a ground plane is present.

text: The rear combination lamp ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
applies_to: LED electronics / PCB(s) and electrical connector of rear position, stop and reversing functions
test_case: Test per Annex 10 paragraph 2 (ISO 7637-2 pulses and ISO 16750-2 starting profile); lamp functions show no unacceptable degradation.

text: Conducted transients from the rear combination lamp ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited.
applies_to: LED electronics / PCB(s) and electrical connector
test_case: Measurement per Annex 10 paragraph 3 (ISO 7637-2) on supply lines; emitted transients within the limits of the Regulation.

text: Test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the rear combination lamp ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
applies_to: Supply lines and connector pins of rear position, stop and reversing lamp electronics
test_case: ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b applied to each supply-connected input (e.g. tail, stop, reverse feeds) with lamp operating; functions remain within the immunity performance criteria.

text: The starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the rear combination lamp ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines (unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).
applies_to: Supply lines and connector pins of rear position, stop and reversing lamp electronics
test_case: ISO 16750-2 starting profile applied to supply-connected inputs with lamp operating; functions remain within the immunity performance criteria. For an M1 lamp not exclusively reserved for electric vehicles, this test applies.

text: Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear combination lamp ESA on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
applies_to: Supply lines and connector pins of LED driver electronics
test_case: ISO 7637-2 conducted transient emission measurement on each supply-connected line during switching of each lamp function; emissions within the applicable limits.

text: Every rear combination lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
applies_to: Housing / outer lens marking area
test_case: Drawing review and visual inspection of the sample: a marking area is reserved that accommodates the approval marking and all markings of paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.

text: All markings on the rear combination lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
applies_to: All markings (housing, outer lens)
test_case: Visual check for legibility, plus a durability check (e.g. rubbing with water- and solvent-soaked cloth): markings remain legible and not removed.

text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the approval marking (arrangement per Annex 7): a >= 5 mm.

text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: circle surrounding "E" followed by the country distinguishing number is present.

text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2., placed close to the approval mark.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: 4- to 6-digit sequential number present and located close to the approval mark; matches the approval number.

text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4. for the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector functions.
applies_to: Approval marking (function symbols)
test_case: Visual inspection against paragraph 3.2.4.: a correct identification symbol is present for each approved function.

text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: Visual inspection: "148R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments in force at the time of approval.

text: As the rear combination lamp is a handed unit which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
applies_to: Approval marking (handed left/right units)
test_case: Visual inspection of both left- and right-hand units: horizontal mounting arrow present.

text: For the rear position lamp, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
applies_to: Rear position lamp marking
test_case: Check the arrow direction on the lamp in its installed orientation: arrow points outwards from the vehicle.

text: If the reversing lamp has reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
applies_to: Reversing lamp marking
test_case: If approved with reduced light distribution: check the arrow in installed orientation points outwards from the vehicle.

text: If the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
applies_to: Approval marking (function symbols)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection shows "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

text: If the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamps system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4.
applies_to: Approval marking (function symbols)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection shows "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol.

text: If a lamp function has reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
applies_to: Approval marking
test_case: If approved with reduced light distribution: visual inspection shows the downward vertical arrow from a horizontal segment.

text: The rear combination lamp shall bear the approval marking.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp
test_case: Visual inspection: approval marking present on the lamp.

text: The rear combination lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp
test_case: Visual inspection: trade name or mark of the applicant present.

text: If the lamp uses replaceable light sources, it shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (replaceable light sources, if any)
test_case: If replaceable light sources are used: visual inspection shows the light source category marking; not required for non-replaceable LED sources.

text: If the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), it shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (LED substitute light sources, if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection shows the LED substitute light source category marking.

text: As the lamp has non-replaceable light sources and/or an electronic light source control gear, it shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp with LED (non-replaceable) light sources
test_case: Visual inspection: rated voltage (e.g. 12V) or voltage range marked on the lamp.

text: If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
applies_to: Replaceable light source module (if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the module for the applicant trade name or mark.

text: If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code, comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1., followed by additional symbols or characters in case several non-identical light source modules are used; the module approval mark and the lamp approval mark shall be from the same applicant.
applies_to: Replaceable light source module (if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the code format "MD" + approval mark without circle (+ distinguishing characters for non-identical modules); verify same applicant as lamp.

text: If replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
applies_to: Replaceable light source module (if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the voltage marking on the module.

text: If replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (with replaceable module)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection that the module code is marked on the lamp.

text: If replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (with replaceable module)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the voltage marking on the lamp.

text: An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
applies_to: External electronic control gear / intensity control (if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection of the external unit for identification number and manufacturer name.

text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
applies_to: Approval marking location (housing / outer lens)
test_case: Drawing review and inspection: marking is on a part permanently joined to the light-emitting outer lens.

text: The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
applies_to: Approval marking location
test_case: Inspection on vehicle or installation mock-up: marking visible with lamp fitted or with boot lid/door opened.

text: If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
applies_to: Outer lens and housing
test_case: If the outer lens is detachable: visual inspection shows the approval marking on both lens and housing.

text: The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp markings
test_case: Visual inspection: all listed markings are affixed on the lamp itself.

text: The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module component.
applies_to: Replaceable light source module (if any)
test_case: If applicable: visual inspection that module markings are on the module.

text: Where a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number is affixed to the combined lamp complying with several UN Regulations, it shall be visible after installation.
applies_to: Single approval mark on combined lamp
test_case: Inspection on vehicle or mock-up: single approval mark visible after installation.

text: Where a single approval mark is used, no part of the combined lamp that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
applies_to: Single approval mark on combined lamp / outer lens
test_case: Design review and disassembly check: removing any light-transmitting part also removes the approval mark.

text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
applies_to: Single approval mark on combined lamp
test_case: Measure mark components and compare with the minimum sizes of each applicable UN Regulation (e.g. R148, R150): not less than the minimum of the smallest individual mark.

text: The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp production (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions and retro-reflector)
test_case: Audit of the manufacturer's conformity of production system and records against 1958 Agreement Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3) and paragraph 6 of UN R148. Pass if the procedures are in place and production samples meet the paragraph 6 requirements.

text: The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear combination lamp intended for installation on M1 vehicles, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp (all signalling functions), installation-related characteristics for M1 vehicles
test_case: Review the lamp design and drawings against UN R48 sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes, using the series of amendments in force at application. Check every requirement that can be verified at lamp type approval, e.g. geometric visibility angles, apparent surface and colour. Pass if all such requirements are met.

text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 sections 5 and 6 pertinent to the rear position lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied to the rear position lamp function, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Rear position lamp
test_case: Check the rear position lamp's geometric visibility and red colour against the UN R48 individual specification for rear position lamps on M1. Check the illuminating surface and orientation of the handed unit, with the opposite-side unit presumed mirrored. Pass if compliant.

text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 sections 5 and 6 pertinent to the stop lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied to the stop lamp function, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Stop lamp
test_case: Check the stop lamp's geometric visibility angles and red colour against the UN R48 individual specification for stop lamps (S1/S2) on M1 vehicles. Pass if compliant.

text: The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 sections 5 and 6 pertinent to the reversing lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied to the reversing lamp function, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
applies_to: Reversing lamp, reversing lamp window/insert in outer lens
test_case: Check the reversing lamp's geometric visibility angles and white colour against the UN R48 individual specification for reversing lamps on M1 vehicles. Pass if compliant.

text: The lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions of the rear combination lamp) shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp: housing, rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, LED PCBs, internal wiring/connector, fasteners/clips
test_case: Design review plus vibration/durability test representative of vehicle use (e.g. per OEM vibration profile); after exposure, all functions (rear position, stop, reversing) operate correctly with no LED failure, intermittent contact, loosened fasteners or mechanical damage.

text: The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.
applies_to: Rear combination lamp: photometric and colorimetric characteristics of rear position, stop and reversing lamps; outer lens; reflector surfaces
test_case: After vibration/durability exposure, repeat photometric and colorimetric measurements per UN R148 requirements; intensities and colour coordinates remain within the prescribed limits for each function.

text: An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as a lamp marked "D" shall only be applied to the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions of the rear combination lamp; the reversing lamp is not eligible for "D" approval.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; Stop lamp
test_case: Design and approval-documentation review: confirm that any "D" marking appears only on the rear position or stop lamp function and not on the reversing lamp. Pass if no "D" approval or marking is applied to the reversing lamp.

text: An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" shall only be applied to the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions of the rear combination lamp; the reversing lamp is not eligible for "Y" approval.
applies_to: Rear position lamp; Stop lamp
test_case: Design and approval-documentation review: confirm that any "Y" marking or interdependent lamp system approval covers only the rear position or stop lamp function. Pass if no "Y" approval or marking is applied to the reversing lamp.

text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source); or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
applies_to: Rear position lamp / stop lamp (reciprocal incorporation, LED light sources)
test_case: Design review of the LED/PCB circuit: confirm that the rear position and stop functions use separate light sources, or that the lamp is intended for a vehicle with a failure tell-tale; pass if either condition is met.

text: If a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp function, only one logo shall be incorporated, and all requirements of this Regulation for that specific function shall be fulfilled.
applies_to: Rear position lamp, outer lens, reflector surfaces
test_case: Visual inspection for the number of logos; photometric and colorimetric tests of the function with the logo per this Regulation; pass if there is one logo and all function requirements are met.

text: Irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3., only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be incorporated in the lamp's optical components or outer lens.
applies_to: Outer lens / optical components (logo)
test_case: Visual inspection of the logo against the vehicle or body manufacturer brand; pass if it is only that brand logo.

text: The enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
applies_to: Rear position lamp logo area on outer lens / optical components
test_case: Measure the projected enclosed logo area in the direction of the reference axis; pass if it is ≤ 100 cm2.

text: The stop lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
applies_to: Stop lamp
test_case: Visual inspection of the stop lamp apparent surface (optical components and outer lens); pass if no logo is present.

text: The reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
applies_to: Reversing lamp, reversing lamp window/insert in outer lens
test_case: Visual inspection of the reversing lamp apparent surface (optical components and outer lens window); pass if no logo is present.

text: In the rear combination lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
applies_to: LED light sources and PCB wiring of rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions
test_case: Review the circuit diagram and PCB layout to identify LED groups wired in series or with common failure behaviour. Disconnect one LED per group and verify that the whole group extinguishes. Pass: each such group is treated as one light source in the failure analysis of paragraph 4.6.1.2.

text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.10.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
applies_to: Rear position lamp
test_case: Option (a): simulate failure of each single light source (or group per paragraph 4.6.1.1.) in turn and measure on a goniophotometer at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass: all minimum intensities are met; with all sources lit, no maximum is exceeded. Option (b): verify that a failure signal is produced for each single failure. Pass: signal is produced and the communication form notes tell-tale-only use.

text: In case of failure of any one light source in the stop lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.7.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
applies_to: Stop lamp
test_case: Option (a): simulate failure of each single light source (or group) in turn and take photometric measurements at the Annex 3 standard light distribution points. Pass: all minimum intensities are met; with all sources lit, maximum values are not exceeded. Option (b): verify that a failure signal output is generated for each single failure. Pass: the signal is produced and the communication form contains the tell-tale note.

text: In case of failure of any one light source in the reversing lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraph 6.4.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.
applies_to: Reversing lamp
test_case: Option (a): simulate failure of each single light source (or group) in turn and take photometric measurements at the Annex 3 grid points. Pass: all minimum intensities are met; with all sources lit, no maximum is exceeded. Option (b): verify that a failure signal is produced for each single failure. Pass: the signal is present and the communication form notes vehicle tell-tale requirement.

text: If the rear position lamp is of category R2, in case of failure of the variable intensity control resulting in emission of more than the maximum value of category R1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
applies_to: Rear position lamp (category R2, variable intensity control electronics)
test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control (e.g. open or short of the control input or driver fault) and measure the luminous intensity. Pass: the lamp automatically reverts to intensities meeting the steady-intensity requirements of category R1.

text: If the stop lamp is of category S2, in case of failure of the variable intensity control resulting in emission of more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
applies_to: Stop lamp (category S2, variable intensity control electronics)
test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and perform photometric measurement. Pass: intensities automatically fall within the steady-intensity requirements of category S1.

text: If the stop lamp is of category S4, in case of failure of the variable intensity control resulting in emission of more than the maximum value of category S3, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
